why.title: Why Vydra?
why.philosophy: Vydra was born out of the need to build scalable applications without the burden of monolithic frameworks. We leverage native platform APIs, avoiding heavy execution times and complex virtual DOMs, letting you focus on real, standard architectures.
why.lit.title: Ultra Lightweight & Lit-Powered
why.lit.description: Powered by Lit. Experience blazing-fast rendering and minimal bundle sizes. We give you a reactive structure without sacrificing performance or developer ergonomics.
why.standards.title: 100% Native Web Standards
why.standards.description: Write standard JavaScript and Web Components natively. Your knowledge transfers, and your code won't become legacy when the next hype cycle arrives.
why.microfrontends.title: Single-SPA & Microfrontends
why.microfrontends.description: Designed from its core for distributed architectures. Seamlessly integrate with single-spa to compose and decouple independent microfrontends effortlessly.
features.title: Engineered for Developers
features.performance.title: Native Performance
features.performance.description: Built on Lit and native Web Components. No heavy runtime, no Virtual DOM — just fast, standards-based rendering.
features.typesafe.title: Type-Safe by Design
features.typesafe.description: Powered by TypeScript and modern ES modules for predictable code, better tooling, and scalable apps.
features.microfrontend.title: Micro-Frontend Ready
features.microfrontend.description: Designed from day one for Single-SPA and distributed frontends. Independent apps, shared architecture.
code.title: Clean API.
code.description: No complex build pipelines. Just import, extend, and render. Vydra leverages Lit-html for the most efficient templating in the browser.
faq.title: Common Questions
faq.react.question: Is it compatible with React/Vue?
faq.react.answer: Yes! Since Vydra produces standard Web Components, you can use them inside any framework.
faq.seo.question: What about SEO?
faq.seo.answer: Vydra supports Server-Side Rendering (SSR) through our hydration kit.

guide.intro.title: Introduction
guide.intro.welcome: Welcome to the Vydra Framework documentation! Vydra is a native web framework designed to create single-spa and microfrontend applications with ease, leveraging the full power of modern web standards. Our mission is to provide a seamless development experience for large-scale enterprise applications where modularity and performance are paramount.
guide.intro.whatIs.title: What is Vydra?
guide.intro.whatIs.p1: Vydra is built on top of Web Components, Lit, and Vite. It is designed to scale within large organizations where multiple teams need to work on the same platform without stepping on each other's toes. By using the browser's native capabilities, we minimize the amount of code shipped to the user and maximize runtime efficiency.
guide.intro.whatIs.p2: One of its core strengths is the use of scoped elements, which ensures perfect style and logic isolation between different parts of your application or different microfrontends. This means you can have multiple versions of the same component library running side-by-side without conflicts, a common challenge in microfrontend architectures.
guide.intro.features.title: Core Features
guide.intro.features.p: Vydra provides a robust set of core libraries to handle every aspect of modern application development. Each module is designed to be lightweight and tree-shakable, ensuring your application stays fast as it grows:
guide.intro.features.bus.title: bus
guide.intro.features.bus.desc: A pub/sub based communication system for seamless interaction between microfrontends and the root orchestrator. It supports scoped events and global message broadcasting.
guide.intro.features.core.title: core
guide.intro.features.core.desc: Essential mixins, utilities, and helpers to speed up the creation of both microfrontend and root applications. It includes lifecycle management and dependency injection.
guide.intro.features.router.title: router
guide.intro.features.router.desc: A lightweight, powerful router designed for both single-page navigation and microfrontend orchestration. It handles nested routes and dynamic loading of modules.
guide.intro.features.forms.title: forms
guide.intro.features.forms.desc: Reactive forms inspired by Angular, bringing structured and type-safe form management to Web Components with powerful validation support.
guide.intro.features.i18n.title: i18n
guide.intro.features.i18n.desc: Built-in internationalization support to manage translations across multiple languages easily, supporting dynamic locale loading and interpolation.
guide.intro.features.http.title: http
guide.intro.features.http.desc: Comprehensive HTTP services for API communication with common methods, interceptor support, and request/response transformation.
guide.intro.next: To fully understand how Vydra works, it's important to grasp the underlying architecture.
guide.concepts.title: Concepts
guide.concepts.intro: To work effectively with Vydra, it's essential to understand the core architectural concepts: Microfrontends, Applications (Single-SPA), and the Root App (Orchestrator). These pillars form the foundation of a scalable and maintainable frontend architecture.
guide.concepts.mfe.title: Microfrontends
guide.concepts.mfe.p1: In Vydra, a microfrontend is a self-contained unit of functionality that can be developed and deployed independently. It serves its own bundle and is eventually consumed by a Root App. This allows different teams to use different technologies or versions of the same technology without affecting the rest of the system.
guide.concepts.mfe.p2: Vydra recommends that each microfrontend generates its own standalone bundle. The Root App only passes configuration to the microfrontend; it never tries to inject dependencies or libraries into them (unless explicitly desired). This ensures a clean separation of concerns and prevents version conflicts.
guide.concepts.apps.title: Apps (Single-SPA)
guide.concepts.apps.p: A Single-SPA in the context of Vydra can be a typical independent application. It can run on its own during development and testing, but it's also ready to be integrated into a larger microfrontend ecosystem. This flexibility allows you to start small and grow into a complex architecture as needed.
guide.concepts.root.title: Root App (Orchestrator)
guide.concepts.root.p: The Root App is the conductor of the orchestra. Its primary responsibility is to orchestrate the different microfrontends, mounting and unmounting them based on the current URL. It also provides global services like authentication, navigation, and the shared event bus.
guide.concepts.routing.title: Routing Strategy
guide.concepts.routing.p1: Vydra uses a decentralized routing approach. Each microfrontend manages its own internal routes, while the Root App remains unaware of them. This allows microfrontends to have complex internal structures without complicating the root configuration.
guide.concepts.routing.p2: When a user navigates, the Root App detects the change and identifies which microfrontend corresponds to the new base path. It then mounts the correct microfrontend, which takes over the routing for its specific segment. This process is seamless and maintains the single-page application experience.
guide.concepts.next: Now that you understand the architecture, you're ready to start building!
